title: Aharonov-Casher-induced electric quadrupole of charge-neutral particles
authors: Hojun Lee, Youngjae Jeon, Suik Cheon, Hyun-Woo Lee
abstract: For charged particles, their orbital angular momentum (OAM) in solid have a direct magnetic manifestation as an orbital magnetization. For charge-neutral particles, however, the physical manifestation of the OAM in solid remains unclear. Here, we show that a charge-neutral particle carrying a magnetic moment couples to electric-field gradient through the Aharonov-Casher (AC) effect, thereby exhibiting the electric quadrupole in crystalline solids. This AC-induced electric quadrupole (AC-EQ) contains the scalar, toroidal dipole, and reduced quadrupole components, which are conjugate to the divergence, circulation, and shear of the electric field, respectively. As representative examples, we calculate the AC-EQ of magnons in two magnetic systems. In ferromagnetic pyrochlore, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) induces a sizable AC-EQ, whereas in helical Fe langasite the AC-EQ emerges from the helical spin configuration even in the absence of DMI. In both systems, the unit-cell-integrated AC-EQ components reach magnitudes comparable to typical nuclear electric quadrupole moments.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a mechanism by which charge-neutral quasiparticles, such as magnons, can exhibit an electric quadrupole moment via the Aharonov-Casher effect. By treating this response semiclassically, the authors calculate the $	ext{AC-EQ}$ tensor and demonstrate its relevance in magnetic materials, showing it is comparable to nuclear moments.
main_problem: The primary goal is to elucidate the physical manifestation of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) for charge-neutral particles in solids, as its magnetic signature is not straightforward.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that a charge-neutral particle with a magnetic moment exhibits an Aharonov-Casher induced electric quadrupole ($	ext{AC-EQ}$) when coupled to the electric field gradient in crystalline solids. These $	ext{AC-EQ}$ components can reach magnitudes comparable to typical nuclear moments.
method: The theory employs a semi-classical framework, deriving the $	ext{AC-EQ}$ tensor as a linear response of thermodynamic potentials (like the grand potential) to spatial derivatives of the electric field.
model_or_system: The analysis is developed for charge-neutral particles, using magnons in magnetic systems like ferromagnetic pyrochlore and helical langasite as concrete examples. The formalism involves effective electromagnetic potentials derived from the particle's magnetic moment coupling.
key_observables: AC-induced electric quadrupole ($	ext{AC-EQ}$), which decomposes into scalar, toroidal dipole, and reduced quadrupole components; Polarization ($	ext{P}_\alpha$).
important_parameters: Magnetic moment ($\mu$), crystalline solid structure (pyrochlore, langasite), and the coupling strength derived from the Aharonov-Casher effect.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on a semi-classical approximation and assumes weak electric fields/slow variations in external potentials.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the intuitive picture of how angular motion generates specific components of the $	ext{AC-EQ}$ tensor, depending on the relative orientation of the magnetic moment ($\mu$) and the rotation vector ($ oldsymbol{\omega}$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the effective potentials (Eqs. 11, 12) and then deriving the $	ext{AC-EQ}$ tensor ($Q_{\alpha eta}$) as a response function (Eq. 19). It decomposes this tensor into irreducible components (Rank-0, Rank-1, Rank-2), providing physical interpretations for each component.
why_interesting: This work extends the concept of orbital magnetism from charged particles to neutral excitations like magnons, predicting measurable electric quadrupole responses that are sensitive to magnetic structure and spin texture.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Intuitive picture of Aharonov-Casher electric quadrupole (AC-EQ). (a) The polarization P induced by the linear motion of a particle carrying the magnetic moment µ. (b), (c) Representative electric-quadrupole components Qαβ generated by the angular motion of a particle carrying µ. (b) The case of µ = µˆz and ω = ωˆz. (c) The case of µ = µˆy and ω = ωˆz.

FIG. 2. Irreducible decomposition of AC-EQ. The three columns represent the rank-0 AC-EM, rank-1 Aharonov- Casher electric toroidal dipole (AC-ETD), and rank-2 reduced AC-EQ (AC-REQ), respectively. The upper panels show the electric-field configurations conjugate to the respective AC- EQ components. The lower panels schematically illustrate the corresponding combinations of the magnetic moment µ and its orbital motion of the particle.

FIG. 3. Crystal structure, DMI dependence, and tempera- ture dependence of the AC-EQ components in ferromagnetic pyrochlore Lu2V2O7. (a) Left: crystal structure of Lu2V2O7 in the conventional unit cell. Right: four-sublattice basis, where the green arrows indicate the directions of the DMI vectors. Only V atoms are shown as spheres. (b) DMI de- pendence of the AC-EM and Q(2) 3z2−r2, calculated at fixed tem- perature T = 60 K. (c), (d) Temperature dependence of the AC-EM and AC-REQ components, respectively. These re- sults are calculated for |D| ≈0.57 meV.

FIG. 4. Crystal structure, magnetic structure, and temper- ature dependence of the AC-EQ components in noncollinear antiferromagnetic Fe langasite Ba3NbFe3Si2O14. (a) Top left: top view of the crystal structure of Fe langasite, where only the Fd atoms are shown. J1 and J2 denote intralayer exchange paths. Top right: interlayer exchange paths J3, J4, and J5. Bottom: helical magnetic structure of Fe langasite. We adopt a commensurate approximation in which seven magnetic lay- ers constitute one magnetic unit cell. The crystallographic a and c axes are chosen as the x and z axes, respectively. (b)–(d) Temperature dependence of the AC-EM, AC-ETD, and AC-REQ components, respectively.
